greeting: Good morning, Bay View, and happy Sunday. The warm spell ends today: a cold front brings rain this morning, then falling temperatures, and tonight drops into the upper 20s. Families, a heads-up for the short week: MPS students have class Monday, then are off Tuesday through Friday for a staff development day and Thanksgiving break.

top.title: The warm spell ends today, and lows in the 20s arrive tonight and Monday night
top.dek: After a record-warm weekend, Thanksgiving week turns colder, with a chance of rain and snow Wednesday night.
top.body:
A cold front crossing southern Wisconsin this morning brings a period of rain to Bay View, according to the National Weather Service in Sullivan. Behind it, winds shift to the northwest and stay gusty this afternoon, and temperatures fall through the 40s.

The change is sharp. Tonight's forecast low is 28 under clearing skies, Monday tops out near 40, and Monday night drops to about 24. Tuesday stays near 40 and sunny. That's a long way from Friday's 67, which broke a 129-year-old record.

Wednesday turns cloudy, and Wednesday night brings a chance of rain and snow with a low near 33. Thanksgiving Day looks gray with a high near 43 and a chance of light rain, the forecast says.

If you've been putting off yard chores, this is the week: the city's leaf rake-out runs through Nov. 29, and winter overnight parking rules start Dec. 1. Disconnect garden hoses before tonight's freeze.

spotlight.title: Spotlight: BC Modern
spotlight.dek: Bay View's once-a-month vintage showroom fills a former credit union with fresh mid-century finds
spotlight.body:
BC Modern is a vintage furniture shop at 3116 S. Chase Ave. with a twist: it opens only one weekend a month. Each sale fills two floors and about 5,000 square feet with mid-century modern and vintage furniture, lighting, decor and collectibles, and every weekend brings an entirely new collection.

It's run by Eric and Veronica Lewis, who describe it as Milwaukee's largest family-operated Black- and Brown-owned vintage store. The shop grew out of their auction businesses: We Bay Auctions, an eBay consignment service started in 2005, and Brew City Auctions, a full-service estate liquidation company added in 2011. BC Modern followed in 2015. In 2021 they bought the Chase Avenue building, built in the 1960s as Nordberg Credit Union, and FOX6 covered the grand reopening there in September 2022 after about six months of renovation.

Most pieces come straight from private estates and collectors. Only the best make the showroom floor; the rest go through the couple's live and online auctions. The shop says everything is cleaned, and refinished or reupholstered when needed, before it's priced. Expect sectionals, credenzas, lamps, barware and glass, plus CeCe's Candy Shop, a nostalgic candy counter on the garden level.

The once-a-month format draws a crowd: Shepherd Express reported in May that more than a thousand shoppers come through on a sale weekend. This month, Midwest Living picked BC Modern as Wisconsin's best vintage shop in its state-by-state roundup. The business also buys estates, offers styling services and sells gift cards and a VIP membership with early access.

Its recent posts preview the November Collection: a magenta sectional, a couch and chair in fresh upholstery, vintage Christmas decor and glowing ceramic trees. The sale runs Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 28 and 29, with VIP early access Friday evening. December's sale moves up to Dec. 12-13 because of the holidays.

BC Modern, 3116 S. Chase Ave. Open the last full weekend of each month (Dec. 12-13 in December), Saturday and Sunday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. bcmodernmke.com, @bcmodernmke on Instagram.

buzz.headline: Got a payment request from the Bike Fed? Don't click it
buzz.body: The Wisconsin Bike Fed, headquartered on Becher Street, warned on Facebook this week that emails made to look like they come from one of its staff and asking for payments are a spoof or a hack. history.title: The Llewellyn Library: Bay View's hilltop branch on Russell Avenue
history.text: In 1914, Bay View got its first purpose-built library: the Henry Llewellyn Branch on Russell Avenue, on land donated by Llewellyn's sons. It served the neighborhood until 1993.
history.body:
For its first decades, Bay View's library kept moving. MPL dates the neighborhood's library to Beulah Brinton's lending shelves of the 1870s; after Bay View joined Milwaukee in 1887, its library became the Milwaukee Public Library's first branch, at what is now 2457 S. Wentworth Ave. (today the home of Goodkind). It later moved twice along Kinnickinnic Avenue, in about 1896 and again in 1908.

In 1913, Silas J. and John T. Llewellyn donated a lot on Russell Avenue in honor of their father, Henry Llewellyn. The Henry Llewellyn Branch opened there in 1914, built with a $30,000 city bond and designed by Milwaukee architects Van Ryn & DeGelleke in a Neoclassical style. The Wisconsin Historical Society calls it the first neighborhood library the city built for its system. It sat on a rise above the street, reached by a grand stair, and opened with fewer than 1,000 books.

By 1958 the collection topped 10,000 volumes and had nowhere to go. A $150,000 remodeling designed by Grassold & Johnson opened in 1959: crews removed the grand stair, dug away the hill to turn the basement into the main floor, and added a modern one-story wing across the front. The library ran from the former Bay View Baptist Church next door during the work.

The branch served Bay View until 1993, when the current library opened in its wedge-shaped building at 2566 S. Kinnickinnic Ave. The old building was leased to Milwaukee Public Schools, which used it for Bay View High School's Redcat Academy, then sat empty. The city put it up for sale in 2024, and this fall it picked a developer to turn it into apartments. The name "Henry Llewellyn Branch Library" is still carved in the stone frieze.
